earlier_scan.source_named: Only Glottolog's most extensive description is Laycock 1973 (1-page a wordlist or less); no grammar or phonology exists per Glottolog

sources.citation: Foreman, Velma & Helen Marten. 1978. Yessan-Mayo phonemes. Ms., SIL (archives 31302), 31 pp.
sources.note: For Yessan-Mayo (yess1239), not Pasi: 'Stress is predictable, and therefore, non-phonemic.. 1. The first syllable of a word which contains /a/ is stressed, 2. When there is no syllable containing /a/ in a word, the first syllable of the word is stressed.' Not transferred to Pasi.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid pasi1259 (and parent node mayo1278 'Mayo-Pasi'); Glottolog 5.1 CLDF sources.bib a full-text search for stress/accent [psq]/pasi1259
sources.note: No grammar/phonology/sketch reference exists; Pasi-tagged items are Hutchinson 1981, Laycock 1973, Laycock Notebook D8 (ms wordlist 'Pasi (also with Pahi in a separate column)'), Ethnologue.

sources.citation: OLAC: Resources in and about the Pasi language [psq] (capture 2021-01-15)
sources.note: Inventory only: Laycock Notebook D8 (PARADISEC DL2-019), Hutchinson 1981, Ethnologue, Glottolog, LINGUIST List. No description listed.

sources.citation: Hatfield, Adam. 2016. A grammar of Mehek. PhD dissertation, University at Buffalo (SUNY). (sec. 1.2-1.3, pp. 4-5)
sources.note: Nothing on Pasi; p.5 states: 'None of the other Tama languages have a grammatical description or other material, though Pahi and Pasi are briefly covered in an SIL survey article (Hutchinson 1981).' (Its stress section, 3.8, is for Mehek only.)

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. [captures 2014-2022]. NewGuineaWorld: 'Pasi' (page under Sepik River > Middle Sepik River > Ma-Tama > Tama > Pasi-Yamano), with parent pages 'Pasi-Yamano' and 'Tama'. sites.google.com/site/newguineaworld (classic Google Sites; live site now behind Google sign-in).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Nothing: the Pasi page, the Pasi-Yamano page and the Tama page are empty placeholder tiles ('sites-layout-empty-tile') in every Internet Archive copy size class (33-41 KB = site chrome only); no text, no source list, no phonology.

sources.citation: Easton, Catherine. [c. 2003]. Alphabet Design Workshops in Papua New Guinea: A Community-Based Approach to Orthography Development. Conference paper, SIL-PNG; PDF (14 pp.) in SIL International's REAP repository (file).
sources.note: Nothing language-specific. The only prosody content is generic ADW procedure: 'As well as individual phones, phonological features such as tone, stress, and nasalisation, and patterns in the language such as word breaks are discussed.' (p.7). No Pasi data anywhere in the paper.

sources.citation: Sumbuk, Kenneth Memson. 1999. Morphosyntax of Sare. PhD thesis, University of Waikato. xiii+335 pp. (hdl 10289/13888). Ch.1 with Chart 1.1 'The position of Sare within the Sepik area Papuan languages (Laycock 1973)'; 2.2.1 Stress (pp.40-42) for Sare/Kapriman only.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Read held by the project: the thesis describes Sare (Kapriman, kapr1245) only; p.2 'Of the Sepik Hill Family, to which Sare belongs, only Alamblak (Bruce 1984), has a comprehensive description'; the explicit stress rule (2.2.1, pp.40-42: secondary stress initial, primary stress final in disyllables and penultimate in longer words) is for Sare alone; nothing on this language.

sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A linguistic bibliography of the New Guinea area (Pacific Linguistics D-90). Canberra: Australian National University. hdl:1885/146624. Language index s.v. 'Pasi (W Sepik; also Besi?)', 'Mayo', 'Mayo-Pasi'.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Bibliography only: confirms that as of 1996 the entire literature on Pasi was Laycock 1973 (checklist), Wurm & Hattori 1981 (atlas) and Hutchinson 1981 (survey) -- no unpublished SIL phonology ms is indexed for Pasi (contrast Yessan-Mayo, which has Foreman & Marten entries). Extract saved, 26 MB PDF not.

sources.citation: Hutchinson, Ian. 1981. A sociolinguistic survey of Heyo, Pahi, and Mayo-Pasi. In R. Loving (ed.), Sociolinguistic surveys of Sepik languages (Workpapers in Papua New Guinea Languages 29), 109-140. Ukarumpa: SIL. SIL archives 23824.
sources.note: The only publication that treats Pasi at all (32 pp.); a survey report, so a stress statement is unlikely, but it may carry a wordlist with stress marks or a short phonological note. Open PDF exists but sil.org is could not be reached by automated download for scripted fetchers and the file was never captured by the the Internet Archive; a browser download would settle it in minutes.
sources.venue: Sociolinguistic surveys of Sepik languages (Workpapers in Papua New Guinea Languages 29)

sources.citation: Hutchinson, Ian. 1980. Pasi word list. Unpublished Standard SIL Survey Word List (106 items as modified by Loving 1980), Yimin village; SIL, Ukarumpa. Transcribed (71 items, ASJPcode) as wordlist 'PASI_2' in Wichmann, S., E. W. Holman, C. H. Brown, M. S. Dryer & Q. Ran (eds.), The ASJP Database, compiled by Matthew S. Dryer.
sources.note: Nothing: ASJPcode transcription omits stress and tone by design. Value is as a pointer -- an unpublished 1980 SIL survey wordlist of Pasi exists (SIL-PNG survey files / L&C Archives, not in OLAC) and the original phonetic sheet may carry stress marks; the ASJP transcription is open (CC-BY).
sources.venue: The ASJP Database, compiled by Matthew S

sources.citation: Foreman, Velma. 1978. Yessan-Mayo dialect survey. Ms., SIL Ukarumpa, 7 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives; PDF issued 2007)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; sec. 2.1 lists Yessan-Mayo phonemes and a glottal-stop note for the Yaawu dialect. Survey covers River and Yaawu dialect villages only; Yimin/Pasi is not included.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU. (entry 77 PASI (Besi), pp. 22-23)
sources.note: Nothing. Entry gives village (Yimin), test list DCL70, and: 'Very closely related to Mayo, and may in fact form part of the Yau dialect of that language.'

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. n.d. [c. 1970]. Notebook D8: Ali, Kalou, Pasi, Olo (PARADISEC DL2-019) -- Pasi list transcribed (26 items, ASJPcode) as wordlist 'PASI' in The ASJP Database, compiled by Matthew S. Dryer.
sources.note: Nothing (ASJPcode has no stress). Confirms the D8 Pasi list is legible and was consulted by Dryer; Laycock's original phonetic notation (which often marks stress) remains behind the PARADISEC login.
